summary.headline: Pitti Engineering FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR1,953 crore and adjusted EBITDA 20% to INR326 crore, with a new INR290 crore casting capex announced.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 7% YoY to INR506 crore, but export shipments slipped as roughly INR20 crore of sales (largely export laminations and machine components) could not be dispatched in March due to container and energy disruptions. Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 17% from 15.9%, though Q4 margins were hit by a mid-quarter energy and commodity spike. Management announced a greenfield casting facility in Hyderabad (INR290 crore, casting capacity to 36,000 tons by Q1 FY30) and said Q1 FY27 will not be worse than Q4 but will not see a sharp recovery. Net debt is about INR570 crore, with a working-capital release of about INR125 crore expected.

segments.name: Traction motor and railway components
segments.commentary: 33% of FY26 revenue, down from 38% per analyst; Q4 absolute sales about INR165 crore vs INR178 crore a year earlier, attributed to about INR20 crore of export shipments slipping (Wabtec, Siemens Mobility).

segments.name: Power generation
segments.commentary: 15% of FY26 revenue; management describes demand as stable across DG sets, thermal and hydro plants.

segments.name: Mining, oil and gas
segments.commentary: 6% of FY26 revenue; cited as a growth area in new product development.

segments.name: Renewable energy (wind)
segments.commentary: 3% of FY26 revenue; growth moderated but offset by data centers and industrial motors.

segments.name: Data centers
segments.commentary: 3% of FY26 revenue; three new data-center programmes added, with commercial revenue expected from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Lamination and assemblies volume
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 18,400 tons (+7.3% YoY); FY26 volume 69,517 tons (+10% YoY), with assemblies growing faster than loose lamination.

segments.name: Raw casting and machine components volume
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 2,783 tons, with temporary year-end softness; FY26 volume 12,012 tons (+15.4% YoY).

guidance_outlook: FY27 targets: lamination sales of about 78,000 tons (about 72% of stated capacity) and machine components of about 16,000 tons; management estimates about INR2,300 crore top line at current commodity prices.
Consolidated lamination capacity is about 108,000 tons (no standalone/subsidiary split); no further lamination capex announced, and current capacity is sufficient to about FY28.
Q1 FY27 expected to be slightly slower than Q4 for both machine components and laminations, and not worse than Q4; no sharp recovery expected in Q1.

Working capital release of about INR125 crore expected as payables rise; net debt seen falling to about INR470 crore before current-year cash generation, and about INR250 crore by FY29 without further lamination capex.
Effective tax rate expected to remain around 33% for FY27 and FY28 due to ESOP, forex hedge accounting and depreciation differences; management did not give PAT guidance.

Maharashtra investment promotion subsidy (on about INR400 crore invested in Aurangabad over four years) may begin in FY27 under a 7-year recovery plan; company is seeking a 9-year plan or may defer accounting by one year.
ESOP cost of about INR10.3 crore per year continues in FY27 and then tapers off; a schedule is to be posted on the website.
capex_capacity: New greenfield casting and machine components facility in Hyderabad, adjacent to existing foundry, at INR290 crore; expected commissioning by Q1 FY30 (2 to 2.5 years), adding 11,400 tons and taking casting capacity to 36,000 tons.

Machine hour capacity to rise from 720,000 to 1.08 million hours, phased in from FY28 and FY29; about INR110-120 crore of the INR290 crore goes to the foundry and the rest to machining centres; allocation about 30% land and civil, 70% plant and machinery; asset turn about 1.2x.

Earlier capex (announced last year, INR150 crore): about INR100 crore spent as of 31 March 2026, with about INR50 crore pending; expected operational by end H1 FY27, debottlenecking casting capacity to 24,000 tons.
Capex funding: about INR100 crore from internal accruals, balance through net debt.
Q4 FY26 utilisation: sheet metal 80%, machining 87%, casting 64%; FY26 full year: sheet metal 76%, machining 81%, casting 71%.
demand_pricing: Quarterly price-change mechanism with international clients passes currency and commodity moves through; management says currency depreciation does not lift margins but helps India's cost competitiveness versus China.
Steel price exposure is managed by one month of raw material inventory and quarterly pricing offset; management says commodity hedging is not needed, while forex is 100% hedged.

Per-ton economics given: loose lamination about INR1.70-1.80 lakh/ton selling price; high value-added assembly about INR2.20-2.30 lakh/ton; raw casting EBITDA about INR30,000-35,000/ton; machined casting EBITDA about INR80,000-1 lakh/ton; loose lamination EBITDA about INR15,000-18,000/ton; high value-added assembly EBITDA about INR30,000-60,000/ton.
Mix: machine components about 80% export, 20% domestic; high value-added assemblies about one-third to 40% export; stator frame and rotor shaft assemblies roughly 50:50.
Management sees FY28 lamination volume of about 90,000 tons, of which about 60,000 tons loose and low value-added assemblies.

Export and new-customer pipeline: a competitor of an existing customer on a new export product from Q3 FY27; data-center casting and assemblies for Caterpillar, with commercial revenue expected from Q3 FY27; Progress Rail added as a customer; Siemens Mobility served via Dakshin Foundry; Alstom is an existing Indian customer.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR290 crore greenfield capex for existing or new products, and what is the roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is for similar products (castings from 50 kg to 4 tons), targeting larger castings for mining, off-highway and data-center applications; machining expansion is modular from FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Why did export revenue decline YoY in Q4, and when will the delayed sales be recognised?
qa_highlights.answer: Foundry output fell from 1 March due to petroleum product (LPG) shortages, and containers were not moving in most of March, so about INR20 crore of mainly export sales slipped; recovery in Q1 will be a slog.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 outlook for volume, revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 targets of 78,000 tons lamination and 16,000 tons machine components, about INR2,300 crore revenue at current commodity prices; margins expected at similar percentages, with higher commodity prices lifting revenue but lowering percentage margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin fall about 100 bps despite the BCIPL ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR20 crore of higher-value sales were stuck in inventory without margin recognition, and a sharp mid-quarter energy-cost spike occurred after the quarterly price change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt trajectory and debt-free plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR570 crore now, falling to about INR470 crore after INR125 crore working-capital release, and about INR250 crore by FY29 without further lamination capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the effective tax rate about 30-33%, and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by non-deductible ESOP cost, uncrystallised forex losses on hedge accounting and depreciation differences; expected to persist for a couple of years, falling only slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the company not hedge commodities, and how does pricing work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says forex is 100% hedged and commodity hedging is unnecessary: one month of raw material inventory is consumed at prior-quarter cost, and customer prices reset one month later (1 May for Q1 FY27).

risks_watch: Energy (LPG) and West Asia disruptions; management says the energy situation is not fully normalised and Q1 FY27 will be slightly slower.
Export logistics: container movement and shipping constraints delayed about INR20 crore of sales in March 2026.
Timing and depreciation of machine-hour capex: machine delivery and ramp-up pace, lease-financed machines, and capitalisation dates are uncertain; no PAT guidance given.
Maharashtra subsidy recovery: 7-year plan may be too heavy versus Maharashtra sales; a 9-year plan or one-year deferral is under negotiation.
Working-capital release of INR125 crore depends on resuming inventory consumption and payables rising; inventory held near INR390-400 crore versus earlier INR300 crore target.
Data-center and Caterpillar programmes and the non-ferrous/ aerospace expansion are at development or sampling stage; commercial revenue expected from Q3 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth, value-add mix and capex, but cautious and evasive on near-term timing: Q1 FY27 recovery, PAT guidance, and energy-driven volatility were repeatedly left open.
